clue.text: Put up defence to tie game

parts.note: a tied match is a draw
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A team builds its defence to hold out for a drawn match.
explanation.walkthrough: A drawbridge is a castle defence that is raised, or put up, against attackers.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle's raisable bridge serves as a barrier that is hoisted to keep enemies out.

clue.text: Sudden moves in board' game

explanation.surface: A sudden play in a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: To dart is to move suddenly, and the pub game of throwing at a dartboard has the same name.

clue.text: Large island in a lake in.European country

indicators.note: in places the article and the lake abbreviation within the country's name

parts.note: Austria is a European country
L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A big island sitting in a lake somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts AL inside AUSTRIA. Australia is sometimes called the world's largest island.
explanation.definitionFit: The continent-sized landmass is often described as an island in its own right.

clue.text: Second's providing support deceitfully

explanation.surface: An assistant who backs someone up does so treacherously.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming second puts one in a trailing place, and support is backing; the phrase also means secretly and treacherously.

clue.text: At home with the newspapers, but coming out soon

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
the press is the newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: Someone at home reading the papers, with a publication due shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: A book being printed is about to be published, so it will appear shortly.

clue.text: Got idea developed for 'showy annual

indicators.note: developed means the letters of the two words are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A gardener's idea grows into a bright flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Godetia is a garden flower grown each year for its bright blooms.

clue.text: Returned instrument to march with

indicators.note: returned means the brass instrument's name is read from right to left

parts.note: a tuba is a brass instrument

explanation.surface: A bandsman brings back his instrument to march with in the parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' turns TUBA round. To march with is to share a border, as one estate marches with another.
explanation.definitionFit: Lands that march with each other share a boundary, which is to adjoin.

clue.text: Colonel's aircraft

definitions.meaning: the cartoon officer's name, with the 's read as 'is'

explanation.surface: An army officer's flying machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonel Blimp was a pompous cartoon officer in a British newspaper, and an airship carrying the same name is a non-rigid dirigible.

clue.text: Reference book, therefore, about 21's twin? Right

indicators.note: about means the word for therefore goes round the twin and the right abbreviation

parts.note: thus means therefore
Jacob's twin brother in Genesis was Esau

explanation.surface: Looking something up about a Biblical twin in a reference work.
explanation.walkthrough: Entry 21 is JACOB, the Biblical patriarch whose twin brother was the hunter, so the cross-reference supplies his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A book listing synonyms is a standard reference work for writers.

clue.text: Harrow, for the first time, to be innovative

explanation.surface: Ploughing a field never tilled, as a fresh venture.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrowing fresh soil is literally opening up untouched earth; figuratively the phrase means doing something pioneering.

clue.text: Fruit giving wine a bit of body

parts.note: rosé is a pink wine
the hip is part of the body

explanation.surface: A drink that adds some body to the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The red seed pod of a wild briar is a fruit used in syrups.

clue.text: Rodents in sleeping quarters freeze.

parts.note: a dorm is a dormitory, where people sleep
to ice is to freeze

explanation.surface: Mice in a chilly dormitory.
explanation.definitionFit: These small hibernating creatures are rodents like mice and squirrels.

clue.text: Most unusual compass, in two ways

indicators.note: in means the word for compass sits between the two road abbreviations

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way; two of them are needed
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way; two of them are needed
compass means scope or range

explanation.surface: A navigator's compass oddly pointing two ways at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compass' looks like the navigating tool but here means scope or extent, and the two ways are both streets.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of odd describes whatever is most peculiar of all.

clue.text: Top mark achievable in final phase

indicators.note: achievable in means the letters can be got from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A student can earn the highest grade in the last stage of the course.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpha is the highest grade an examiner awards, as in alpha plus.

clue.text: Greeting that man will love to get

parts.note: he'll is short for he will
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A man promising to welcome his sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: A word said on meeting someone is a salutation.

clue.text: In Oxford Street, dodges' merry .making

parts.note: in Oxford the main street is known as the High
to jink is to dodge, so jinks are dodges

explanation.surface: Revellers ducking and weaving in an Oxford street.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford's High Street is called simply the High; Oxford Street is also a famous London shopping street, which is the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Boisterous fun and frolics are revelry.

clue.text: Preventer of leaks is more loyal

explanation.surface: Someone who stops leaks is more faithful.
explanation.definitionFit: A stauncher stems a flow such as blood or water; staunch means steadfast, so the comparative is more steadfast.

clue.text: Time for witches — another spell for 14ac to consider

parts.note: entry 14 across, a greeting, has an alternative spelling with an A in place of the E
to ween is an old word meaning to think or consider

explanation.surface: A witch's night calls for a fresh incantation to think about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spell' looks like witchcraft but means spelling. WEEN is archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: October 31st is the night when witches and ghosts are traditionally abroad.

clue.text: Unofficially informative fruit-producer

explanation.surface: A plant that bears fruit also passes on rumours.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing something on the rumour mill is learning it informally; the climbing plant bears bunches of wine fruit.

clue.text: Has-been's confession in deadlock

explanation.surface: A faded star admits to being stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone past it might admit to being out of date; read as one word it is a stalemate.

clue.text: Investigate and record knowledge about unknown quantity

indicators.note: about means the extended-play record abbreviation goes round the algebra letter

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
x is the classic unknown in algebra
lore is traditional knowledge

explanation.surface: A researcher examines and writes down what is known about a mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' applies only to the record, which wraps the algebra letter before the knowledge follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To probe or survey something is to look into it.

clue.text: A learner among three-quarters in Rugby stronghold

indicators.note: among means the article and learner sign go in between the three compass letters

parts.note: three of the four compass points, west, east and south
L is the learner-driver plate letter

explanation.surface: A novice joins the three-quarter line in a rugby team.
explanation.walkthrough: Three-quarters are backs in rugby, but here they are three of the four cardinal points. Wales is a nation famous for its rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: The principality where rugby union is the national sport is a heartland of the game.

clue.text: Sheepish type who tricked hunter

explanation.surface: A timid fellow who fooled a huntsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A piebald sheep breed bears the patriarch's name, and in Genesis he cheated his hunter brother of his birthright.

clue.text: Fielder caught a number of balls

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
in cricket an over is a set of six balls

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder takes a catch during an over.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover is a fielding position in cricket, on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: The player in the cover position is a fielder named for that place.

clue.text: Daily grind? Clerical occupation

parts.note: a daily is a newspaper
grind means hard work

explanation.surface: Office drudgery as the everyday slog.
explanation.definitionFit: Clerks spend their days on forms and documents, the admin of an office.

clue.text: Girl in pool

explanation.surface: A young woman in a swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, and a shared fund of money, as the stakes in a card game.

clue.text: Rabbits with all the virtues?

explanation.surface: Rabbits as paragons of goodness.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbits are poor players or beginners; split as 'no vices' it describes the faultless.

clue.text: Work fast outside university to get rich

indicators.note: outside means the work and fast words go round the university letter

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Working hard and fasting at college to become wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like speed but means a period of abstinence; 'outside' wraps both pieces round the university letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavish wealth and luxury describe something affluent.

clue.text: Rescue vessel on South Island

indicators.note: on means the vessel follows the compass letter

parts.note: Noah's ark saved the animals from the flood

explanation.surface: A lifeboat off a southern island.
explanation.walkthrough: Sark is one of the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Channel isle lying near Guernsey is a landmass surrounded by sea.

clue.text: New pence Neddy needed for 27, say

indicators.note: new means the letters of pence and Neddy form a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A donkey requires new money for its keep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges PENCE NEDDY. Sark is a Crown dependency in the Channel Islands; Neddy is a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A territory governed by but not part of a larger state is like Sark under the British Crown.
